response.query: What compute and reproducibility commitments (GPU type and hours, RAM, storage, exact splits, seeds, config format, code and checkpoint release timeline) are realistic for the project?
response.answer: For realistic compute commitments, use a high-end GPU, 32GB RAM, 500GB storage, 80/10/10 train/validation/test splits, random seeds, and release code and checkpoints within 6 months.

results.title: An Empirical Study of Testing Machine Learning in the Wild
results.content: *   [An Empirical Study of Testing Machine Learning in the Wild](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463). *   [2.1 Related Works on Testing ML Software Systems](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463#sec-2-1). *   [2.1.1 ML Testing Strategy.](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463#sec-2-1-1). *   [2.1.2 ML Testing Properties.](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463#sec-2-1-2). *   [4.2.2 Comparing the Tested ML Properties across Software Systems.](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463#sec-4-2-2). *   [4.3 RQ3: What Are the Software Types of Testing Used in an ML Workflow?](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463#sec-4-3). *   [Lesson Learned from the Studied ML Properties and Testing Strategies](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463#sec-5-1-1). ML engineers often resort to strategies like **Oracle approximation (OA)** [[98](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463#Bib0098)], which allows for slight differences between computed results and the oracle, rather than specifying exact values for tests. Similar to traditional software systems, ML engineers employ numerous testing types, including unit tests, integration tests, and manual tests, throughout the development process [[1](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463#Bib0001)]. In the context of ML-based software systems, ML properties are essential to ensure that the models generalize as expected in deployment scenarios [[18](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463#Bib0018)]. [[51](https://dl.acm.org/doi/full/10.1145/3680463#Bib0051)] proposed a metric-based testing approach for measuring fairness in ML software systems.
